sources.title: Solvari homepage
sources.description: Advertises homeowner matching and the Joost AI assistant. The public interface establishes the assistant’s existence, not its model provider or internal design.

sources.title: Solvari investment
sources.description: Lists a 2018 buyout and current investment; reports more than 60% recurring revenue and support for five strategic acquisitions. No reporting period is stated for the revenue mix.

sources.title: About Solvari
sources.description: Reports 2+ million successful applications, 6,004 affiliated specialists, and 100+ employees. These are undated page counters, not annual volumes or measured active users.

sources.title: Solvari Pro offer
sources.description: Describes professional demand access, account support, company profiles, and communication with leads.

sources.title: Packages and credit bundles
sources.description: Shows package-dependent marketplace and campaign access, CRM, APIs, support, and credit bundles. Starter presentation and bundle arithmetic are ambiguous; no universal tariff is encoded.

sources.title: User terms
sources.description: Positions Solvari as an intermediary; the work agreement is directly between user and professional. Discusses matching parameters, AI support, and human review.

sources.title: Professional terms
sources.description: Defines packages, campaigns, credits, lead pricing, and the effective order form. Access does not guarantee a won job or investment return.

sources.title: Privacy statement
sources.description: Explains project and property data, recipient sharing, automated matching, review rights, and data-use purposes. Describes up to four professionals with more at the user’s request.

sources.title: Trust and professional checks
sources.description: Describes business registration, identity/contact checks, blacklist screening, and experience feedback. These checks do not establish a guarantee of workmanship.

sources.title: Affiliate programme
sources.description: Offers embedded forms and API submission, compensation per lead, a dashboard, and monthly payment; covers Dutch and Belgian demand.

sources.title: Offerte.nl acquisition announcement
sources.description: Places Offerte.nl inside the group and names earlier acquired brands. Calls this the sixth acquisition in three years; a EUR 40m 2024 revenue statement is a forecast, not realized revenue.

items.title: A useful match is the value event
items.summary: Public flow evidence describes a request leading to professional contact and user choice.
items.implication: Modeling inference: optimize verified useful conversations with outcome-observation coverage; do not equate a request with a completed project.

items.title: Guidance creates an editable handoff
items.summary: Joost is offered on the homepage as a way to clarify a home project.
items.implication: Modeling inference: separate assistant draft, user-confirmed brief, and qualification; evaluate material corrections before expanding categories.

items.title: Recurring participation needs demonstrated value
items.summary: Vortex describes recurring revenue as more than 60% of the total without specifying the measurement period.
items.implication: Modeling inference: connect professional renewal to observed demand economics and workflow value; the reported mix is not a cohort retention baseline.

items.title: A package and a lead are different commercial objects
items.summary: Public Pro materials distinguish packages, credits, campaigns, CRM, and API options.
items.implication: Modeling inference: use effective contract versions and entitlement checks; validate the order form instead of hard-coding the ambiguous pricing page.

items.title: The buyer and the daily lead user need different feedback
items.summary: The Pro offer includes communication, CRM, and API connections alongside commercial packages.
items.implication: Role hypothesis: distinguish subscription approval from lead coordination while allowing a small-firm user to occupy both roles.

items.title: Trust evidence must respect the contracting boundary
items.summary: User terms keep the work agreement between the customer and professional; the trust page describes platform checks.
items.implication: Modeling inference: label review provenance and verification scope; route workmanship disputes without promising contract adjudication or project refunds.

items.title: Allocation has a permission and contact dimension
items.summary: The privacy statement explains purpose-specific use and limited recipient sharing; user terms discuss ranking and human review.
items.implication: Modeling inference: record actual recipients, effective permissions, and matching context; provide review and controlled rematching.

items.title: Partner value depends on an explained payable decision
items.summary: Solvari offers forms, APIs, per-lead compensation, reporting, and monthly affiliate payment.
items.implication: Modeling inference: carry stable origin IDs through qualification and settlement, with distinct submitted, accepted, payable, and paid states.

items.title: Acquired brands create continuity requirements
items.summary: Solvari’s 2024 announcement identifies Offerte.nl as an acquisition and references earlier group brands.
items.implication: Modeling inference: treat acquired brands as integration context rather than independent rivals; preserve identity, agreement, credit, and data-use lineage. Acquisition totals across the inspected pages use unreconciled scope.

items.title: Company counters cannot calibrate this operating model
items.summary: Solvari reports application, affiliated-specialist, and employee counters without a dated internal funnel or team breakdown.
items.implication: Modeling inference: keep KPI baselines unknown and staffing explicitly proposed. Gather category, region, cohort, case, and operational load before prioritizing investment.
